Fact.Name: Return files Form 8582
Fact.Description:
True when the modeled passive pool has an overall loss or a current-year passive loss suspended by §469, AND this form's own bottom line resolves. Activity-specific filing exceptions and passive-credit-only filers remain outside the gate.
TWO POINTS, both of them pinned by fixtures: * the first disjunct tested the WRONG SIGN. /overallPassiveNet is signed (the witness reads line 3 straight off it at -42,000), so GreaterThan($0) asked whether the pool had passive INCOME while this Description said "overall loss". It is LessThan($0) now, which is what the Description always claimed and what "Who Must File" means. * IsComplete-FIRST, the RENDER-GATES guarded-presence shape. The gate used to read Complete true over a wholly unanswered Form 8582, so the return would attach a form whose lines 6-11 are all blank. /form8582Line11TotalLossesAllowed is this form's printed total and the one line that proves Part II/III were actually computed; requiring it means a blank Form 8582 is never emitted. Pinned by form8582-line6-unanswered (gate false while the §469 pool still shows its loss) against form8582-line6-line9-example and form8582-line4-smaller-example (both true).
The guard is temporary by construction: once line 6 reads scheduleE:/section8582Magi, line 11 resolves whenever the pool does and the IsComplete leg stops being able to suppress anything.
A SECOND ARM rather than a widening of the first. The two disjuncts above both require an overall passive LOSS or a suspended loss, so a filer with passive activity deductions and an overall passive GAIN got no Form 8582 at all — while the printed line 3 says, of a line that is zero or more, "stop here and include this form with your return", and Who Must File names everyone "who have passive activity deductions (including prior year unallowed losses)". The new arm is exactly that case: line 3 at or above zero AND a loss in either printed leg (line 1d or line 2d). Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/form8582/form8582-whofiles-loss-leg-overall-gain — line 1d a 3,000 loss, line 2d 8,000 of income, line 3 +5,000, suspended 0 — where the gate was measured Complete false before the edit and Complete true after.
WHY IT IS A SEPARATE ARM, NOT A THIRD DISJUNCT INSIDE THE FIRST: the IsComplete(line 11) leg exists so a wholly unanswered Form 8582 is never attached (S3 above), and on a stop-at-line-3 return the form never reaches lines 6 and 10, whose two free writables are what line 11 needs. Requiring line 11 on this arm would make the correction unreachable for the filer it is for. The fixture proves the independence: it removes BOTH /writableForm8582ModifiedAdjustedGrossIncome and /writableForm8582PassiveActivityIncomeTotal, asserts lines 10 and 11 Incomplete, and still asserts the gate Complete true. Part I still prints from scheduleE's exported aggregates, so the attached form is not blank.
NO NEW COMPLETENESS SURFACE: /form8582Line1dRentalActiveSignedNet and /form8582Line2dOtherPassiveSignedNet are derived from scheduleE:/overallPassiveNet and scheduleE:/otherPassiveNet, and the first arm already reads /overallPassiveNet, so this fact depends on nothing it did not already depend on.
WHAT THIS ARM STILL DOES NOT COVER, stated rather than left to be discovered: prior-year unallowed losses (printed lines 1c and 2c) are not modeled in the pool at all, so a filer whose only passive deduction is a carryforward is still not detected here; and a per-activity loss inside a leg that nets positive is invisible to a leg-level test. The first is owned by scheduleE, not by this module.
THE WHO MUST FILE EXCEPTION, CORRECTED by the w13 review. This paragraph used to say the Exception has "six conditions, i8582 lines 42-61" and that THIS ARM "can attach a form the Exception would excuse". Both halves were wrong. The Exception is headed at i8582 line 41 and runs to line 61, and it carries SEVEN bullets, the seventh being the limited-partner / estate-or-trust-beneficiary interest. And this arm cannot reach an excused filer, which is provable from the leg definitions rather than merely untested: the arm fires only when line 2d is a loss, or when line 1d is a loss while the overall net is at or above zero, and the second of those forces line 2d strictly positive. Either way the other-passive leg is non-zero, so passive activities exist that are not rental real estate with active participation, which fails the Exception's FIRST condition by itself.
THE OVER-INCLUSION IS THE FIRST ARM'S, and it is measured, not inferred: tests/nodes/ty2025/form8582/form8582-whofiles-exception-excused-still-files is one actively-participated rental with an 8,000 loss, MAGI 50,000, single, no other passive activity and no prior-year unallowed loss — every Exception condition met — and this gate is Complete true there. It is left that way ON PURPOSE. The harm runs the benign way (an unrequired attachment whose numbers agree with the return; the instructions say the filer does not have to file, not that they must not), while two of the seven conditions (prior-year unallowed losses, current or prior-year unallowed passive credits) have NO facts anywhere in dictionary/ty2025, so modelling the Exception now would hard-code them to "none" and SUPPRESS the form for exactly the filers who must file it. The MAGI condition would additionally have to gate a printed form on ../form8582Line6ModifiedAdjustedGrossIncome, the free writable whose drift from scheduleE:/section8582Magi is an open defect, and the "total loss from the rental real estate activities" condition needs a ruling on whether it means the net of the leg or the sum of the loss activities. dictionary/pdf/2025/gates.tsv already carries the matching render-gate limitation note.
FOURTH CORRECTION, and it is about DECIDABILITY rather than about who files. This is a PRINT gate, so the only two answers it may give are a decided yes and a decided no; a value that is right for the branch it took and silent about whether the branch was the right one is an answer no consumer can act on. The second arm reads the Schedule E pool through ../form8582Line1dRentalActiveSignedNet and ../form8582Line2dOtherPassiveSignedNet, and those aggregates are undecidable on a return whose passive intake is only partly answered - a Schedule K-1 that leaves the item D publicly-traded-partnership question blank leaves scheduleE:/k1PassiveNet undecided and with it /otherPassiveNet and /overallPassiveNet - so on such a return the arm answered the print question with a Placeholder. IsComplete on line 1d is the whole guard: an All returns a decided FALSE as soon as ANY of its operands is a decided FALSE, whatever the operands beside it resolve to, so the guard settles the arm on a decided NO and the two undecidable comparisons cannot lift it back to a Placeholder. It is written FIRST for the reader, not for the evaluator: an All is order-independent, so the position of this member carries no meaning. ONE GUARD COVERS BOTH LEGS: line 1d is line 3 less line 2d, so its completeness is exactly the completeness of both exported aggregates and line 2d needs no guard of its own. AND IT MUST BE LINE 1d, not line 11: the third arm above exists so a stop-at-line-3 filer is detected on a return that never reaches lines 6 and 10, and a line 11 guard here would make that correction unreachable for the filer it is for. NO VALUE MOVES ANYWHERE: wherever this arm resolved a decided TRUE the aggregates were already complete, which is what made the comparison decidable, so the guard is true there by construction.

Fact.Name: Form 8582 Part I line 1d — active-participation rental net
Fact.Description: Overall passive net less the other-passive net. Schedule E exports both aggregate pool values; their difference is the Form 8582 active-participation rental leg.

Fact.Name: Form 8582 Part I line 2d — other passive net
Fact.Description: Schedule E's exported aggregate for all other passive activities.

Fact.Name: Form 8582 Part I line 3 — overall passive net
Fact.Description: Schedule E's exported overall passive net, the combine of lines 1d and 2d.

Fact.Name: Form 8582 Part II line 4 — smaller active-rental loss
Fact.Description: The smaller of the positive loss on line 1d or the overall loss on line 3. The ordinary special-allowance computation is modeled; the prior-year commercial revitalization deduction worksheet is not.

Fact.Name: Form 8582 Part II line 5 — MAGI threshold
Fact.Description:
$150,000, or $75,000 for married filing separately.
DECLARED LIMIT, print fidelity only. The instruction conditions the $75,000 substitution on LIVING APART, not on the filing status alone: "Married persons filing separate returns who lived / apart from their spouses at all times during the year must / enter $75,000 on line 5 instead of $150,000." This Switch reads only filingStatus:/isFilingStatusMFS, so an MFS filer who lived WITH their spouse also gets 75,000 here. NO DOLLAR MOVES: that filer's line 8 is the literal $0 case in ../form8582Line8SpecialAllowanceCap, which does not read line 7, so lines 9 and 11 are unaffected. What is wrong is purely what is PRINTED — dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS8582/en/configuration.yml maps this fact to f1_13[0], so the filer sees a filled-in Part II on a form whose own Caution tells them not to complete Part II.
DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED AT THE FACT LEVEL. The faithful correction is to suppress the whole Part II render (printed lines 4 through 9) for that filer, which is a render-gate concern in dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS8582. Blanking line 5 alone here would leave line 4 populated, i.e. a half-completed Part II, which is worse than a consistently computed one. The same class of print-only infidelity applies to the f8582 line 3 routing note "Line 2d is a loss (and line 1d is zero or more), skip Part II and go to line 10": when the loss sits in the line 2d leg the model still computes and prints lines 4 through 9, and it is numerically harmless for the same reason (line 4 floors to 0 when line 1d is at or above zero, so line 9 is 0 and line 11 equals line 10, exactly what skipping Part II yields).

Fact.Name: Form 8582 Part II line 6 — modified adjusted gross income
Fact.Description:
Enter the line-6 modified adjusted gross income after applying the Form 8582 instructions; the module floors the entered amount at zero.
INTERIM INTAKE, and it is the second MAGI on this return. The return's own §469 allowance is already computed from scheduleE:/section8582Magi — a Derived fact with 18 dependencies — and nothing forces this typed amount to equal it. The consequence is measured, not asserted: in tests/nodes/ty2025/form8582/form8582-line6-magi-drift the filer types $120,000 while scheduleE computes $86,500, so the PRINTED form says the special allowance is $15,000 while the return deducts scheduleE's $25,000 (/rentalSpecialAllowance = /passiveAllowedLossTotal = 25000.00). The companion case form8582-line6-schedulee-magi-agreement pins the only state in which the form is right: the two numbers equal.
THE SUCCESSOR (one line in scheduleE, which block 4 may not edit): add <Export downstreamFacts="true" /> to scheduleE:/section8582Magi and make ../form8582Line6ModifiedAdjustedGrossIncome a bare Dependency on it, retiring this writable. Recorded in the records overlay.

Fact.Name: Form 8582 Part II line 6 — modified adjusted gross income
Fact.Description: The filer-entered modified adjusted gross income, floored at zero — NOT scheduleE:/section8582Magi, which is what the return's own §469 special allowance is computed from. scheduleE carries no <Export downstreamFacts="true" /> on that fact and block 4 may not edit scheduleE, so the intake stands as the interim source and the one-line export is the recorded successor (see ../writableForm8582ModifiedAdjustedGrossIncome for the measured drift and the fixtures that pin it). Part II must not be computed twice; until the export lands it is, and this Description is the place that says so.

Fact.Name: Form 8582 Part II line 7 — threshold less modified AGI
Fact.Description: Line 5 minus line 6, floored at zero as directed when line 6 is at least the threshold.

Fact.Name: Form 8582 Part II line 8 — special allowance cap
Fact.Description:
One-half of line 7, limited to $25,000, or $12,500 for a married filer who files separately and lived apart all year, and $0 for a married filer who files separately and lived with their spouse at any time during the year.
TWO POINTS, both pinned by fixtures: * THE QUESTION IS NO LONGER ASKED TWICE. The MFS case used to read this module's own ../writableForm8582MfsLivedApartAllYear; it now reads filers:/livedApartAllYear, which is the SAME fact scheduleE:/rentalSpecialAllowance reads to decide the allowance the return actually deducts. While the two answers were independent they could disagree, and tests/nodes/ty2025/form8582/form8582-mfs-lived-with-spouse-low-magi (then named for the contradiction it witnessed) measured the disagreement: the form printed a 12,500 special allowance on lines 8, 9 and 11 while /rentalSpecialAllowance was 0.00. The printed form and the deducted allowance now move together by construction, because they read one fact. (The fixture is named for the contradiction it used to witness; now that the writable is retired it no longer answers it and so no longer measures a contradiction, though its asserts are unchanged because they were already driven by filers:/livedApartAllYear.) * THE FORM NO LONGER DISAPPEARS. There was no case for an MFS filer who lived with their spouse, so this line was Incomplete, lines 9 and 11 with it, and the IsComplete leg of ../form8582ReturnFilesThisForm suppressed the whole form for a filer the printed form tells to skip Part II and go to line 10. That filer now gets $0 here, which makes line 9 $0 and line 11 equal to line 10 — exactly what "Instead, go to line 10" means — and the form is filed. Pinned by form8582-mfs-lived-with-spouse.
AN MFS RETURN THAT HAS NOT ANSWERED THE COHABITATION QUESTION leaves this line Incomplete rather than printing a confident $0 over an allowance the return itself cannot resolve. That arm is pinned by form8582-mfs-cohabitation-unanswered, which measures BOTH facts on one return whose filers:/livedApartAllYear is Incomplete, and they DIFFER: THIS line resolves Incomplete (the runner reports it "not in snapshot"), while scheduleE:/rentalSpecialAllowance resolves Placeholder.
THE CAUSE OF THAT DIFFERENCE, isolated by the w13 review. This paragraph used to say the build unit could not name it and offered the Round wrapper or case order as the candidates; both were wrong. It is the Switch evaluator itself (Expression.scala, private object switches, resultRecurse): a case whose When is Incomplete does NOT stop the Switch, because Result.Incomplete carries no value and so falls into the catch-all recursion arm; it only clears the accumulated completeness. The FIRST case whose When has value Some(true) then supplies the result, downgraded with asPlaceholder if any earlier case was undecidable. Result.Incomplete comes back ONLY from running off the end of the case list. So on an MFS return whose filers:/livedApartAllYear is Incomplete: * scheduleE:/rentalSpecialAllowance falls through its undecidable first case and then MEETS its second case, whose When is a bare /isFilingStatusMFS and is Complete(true), so it returns that case's body as a PLACEHOLDER. * THIS fact's three cases are mutually exclusive with no catch-all, so once the non-MFS case is Complete(false) the two MFS cases are both Incomplete, the list is exhausted, and the Switch is Incomplete. The presence of a matching later case is the whole difference. It is not the Round wrapper.
AND THE 0.00 IN THAT FIXTURE IS A COINCIDENCE OF ITS MAGI, which is why the divergence read as harmless. scheduleE's placeholder is its 12,500 branch evaluated, min(12500, one half of max(0, 75000 minus /section8582Magi)), and that fixture inherits wages of 86,500, above the 75,000 ceiling, so the branch is 0.00. form8582-mfs-cohabitation-unanswered-low-magi is the same return at wages 50,000: /section8582Magi Complete 50,000.00, THIS line still Incomplete, and scheduleE:/rentalSpecialAllowance Placeholder 12,500.00 — the full MFS lived-apart allowance handed to a filer whose cohabitation answer is unknown.
THIS LINE'S Incomplete IS THE RIGHT ONE and must not be weakened to match. The consistency successor belongs to scheduleE, which is out of this module's fence and whose change moves a return dollar, so it needs its own unit. IT IS A TWO-CASE CHANGE, AND HALF OF IT IS A TRAP: /rentalSpecialAllowance's second case must test All(isFilingStatusMFS, livedApartAllYear) instead of bare isFilingStatusMFS, AND its third case's When must become Not(isFilingStatusMFS) instead of the bare True catch-all. Doing only the first makes things WORSE, by the same resultRecurse rule: with case 2 undecidable the True catch-all still matches, so the fact would return the NON-MFS branch as a placeholder, min(25000, one half of max(0, 150000 minus magi)) — 25,000.00 at that fixture's MAGI, i.e. the single filer's full allowance handed to an MFS filer, worse than today's 12,500.00. With both cases exclusive the list is exhausted and both facts go Incomplete together, and neither the non-MFS nor the MFS-answered path changes. form8582-mfs-cohabitation-unanswered-low-magi is that change's ready-made witness and goes RED (Placeholder 12,500.00 becomes Incomplete) when it lands. Until then the property that matters still holds: neither the printed line nor the deducted allowance is a confident number there, so the form is never more complete than the return and the gate stays Complete false.
CASE ORDER IS HYGIENE HERE, NOT CORRECTNESS. This paragraph used to claim the non-MFS case must stay FIRST so a non-MFS return never evaluates the cohabitation facts. Measured by mutation in the w13 review: moving it LAST changes no case in the corpus, and it cannot, because AllOperator short-circuits on Result.Complete(false) in both its head position and its accumulator — on a non-MFS return each MFS case's When is Complete(false) without the cohabitation conjunct ever being reached, and without clearing the Switch's accumulated completeness. Keep the order for readability; do not rely on it for completeness.

Fact.Name: Form 8582 Part II line 9 — special allowance
Fact.Description: The smaller of line 4 and line 8. The CRD-specific worksheet can change this amount and remains outside this model.

Fact.Name: Form 8582 Part III line 10 — passive activity income
Fact.Description:
Enter the total of current-year passive net income reported on Part I lines 1a and 2a. Schedule E does not currently export these two positive-income subtotals separately.
The SAME successor as line 6: scheduleE computes the Part I 1a/2a positive-income legs inside its own §469 chain; the export that retires ../writableForm8582ModifiedAdjustedGrossIncome should retire this intake with it, or line 10 stays a free number added to a derived one.

Fact.Name: Form 8582 Part III line 10 — passive activity income
Fact.Description: The filer-entered aggregate of current-year passive net income on Part I lines 1a and 2a.

Fact.Name: Form 8582 Part III line 11 — total losses allowed
Fact.Description: Line 9 plus line 10. This print result is exported as the successor input for Schedule E's future Form 8582 allowable-loss integration.
